aiUseDisclosure: Codex authored branching conversations revealing the challengers as Morrow's own past lives, retained within the crown.

first.question: I knew which stair would creak. I have never been inside this castle.
choices: I used to step over that one.
Someone told you where to put your paws.
responses: And you kept your wooden staff under the bed. How do I know that?
No one came with me. I was afraid you would hear.

kitten.remembered: I remember hiding that staff when the grown cats came home.

second.question: Will you show me how to stand against a sword?
choices: Watch my feet. Jump the low strike.
You can still be afraid. Keep your guard up.
responses: Like this? Then do it again.
I will. Please do not look away.

second.question: Were you this afraid before you wore the crown?
choices: Yes. I thought being king would cure it.
Fear will not stop the blade. Move.
responses: Did it?
Then I had better learn to jump.

first.question: The scar under your left eye. Mine hurts when you touch it.
choices: I got it climbing a broken window.
You copied a scar. That proves nothing.
responses: In winter. The red scarf caught on the latch.
Then why did you reach for your eye before I did?

alley.remembered: There was bread inside the window. We had not eaten for days.

second.question: You remember the window. Do you remember who waited below it?
choices: Someone I promised to feed.
I remember falling. Nothing after that.
responses: You went back for them. Even with the glass in your face.
I remember the street coming up to meet us.

second.question: Look at this scarf before you raise your sword.
choices: I know that knot. I tied it with one paw.
Cloth cannot tell me who you are.
responses: You never learned to loosen it.
It kept the blood off the bread. That was all it had to do.

first.question: Cold water. Iron around one ankle. You tasted it when I came through the door.
choices: There was someone on the other end of the chain.
I have not seen the sea in a thousand years.
responses: A small boat. You would not let it drift away.
You shut your mouth when I lifted the weight. There is still salt on your tongue.

sailor.remembered: The last link broke. The boat reached shore.

second.question: Would you let go this time?
choices: Not while someone was still holding the other end.
I should have cut the rope sooner.
responses: I know. That is why the iron is still here.
You keep remembering a knife. There was no knife.

second.question: Tell me why your ankle aches.
choices: Because I remember the weight.
Because I have stood in this room too long.
responses: Then stand against it once more.
You used to laugh at excuses like that.

first.question: Three bells. You lift your foot before the fourth, though that one has never rung.
choices: The fourth bell broke when I missed the rope.
I can read a rhythm.
responses: You fell into the crowd. You were still laughing.
Then why did you reach for a rope that is not here?

acrobat.remembered: You were afraid of heights. You climbed anyway.

second.question: Do you remember why we climbed so high?
choices: The children below could not afford a seat.
For the applause. I wanted to hear it again.
responses: So you made the whole square a stage.
You always said that. Then you looked down to see if they could see.

second.question: Will you watch my hands or the empty space above them?
choices: Your hands. I have fallen for the other trick.
The place where you must land.
responses: Then you remember more than you admit.
Good. I never did learn to land quietly.

first.question: This needle turns toward your heart. It did that before either of us saw a crown.
choices: I made it to find my way through the dark.
You have put a spell on it.
responses: You held it under your tongue so the cold would not take it.
You spat it into your paw the night your teacher died. No one saw.

witch.remembered: There is still a tooth mark in the silver.

second.question: What were you trying to find?
choices: A house with a light left on.
A way to stop being lost.
responses: The light had gone out before we reached it.
You found the house. That was not the same thing.

second.question: Why do your hands remember how to hold it?
choices: I know the burn it leaves between the claws.
I will not let you put that memory in me.
responses: You used to call that the price of a little warmth.
I did not put it there.

first.question: Your shoulder drops when I lift this shield. The old break never set straight.
choices: I held a gate until the others got through.
I have carried heavier things than your shield.
responses: You counted their footsteps. You stopped at forty-three.
You carried a child through smoke with that arm. It shook for days.

knight.remembered: Forty-three made it through the gate.

second.question: Was the promise worth the arm?
choices: It was worth keeping.
I should have been strong enough to keep both.
responses: Then stop speaking as if you were always a king.
You were strong enough. You stayed too long.

second.question: Put your hand on the break. Tell me you feel nothing.
choices: It still hurts when it rains.
I will not lower my sword for a ghost.
responses: There. An honest answer.
Then make me raise the shield again.

first.question: My mirror shows you without the crown. You will not look at it.
choices: There was a face before this one. I can almost see it.
Turn it over.
responses: Your ears were torn. You hated how the right one folded.
You covered every mirror after the coronation. You knew what was missing.

thief.remembered: You used to press the ear flat before anyone could see.

second.question: Who did you see when you were alone?
choices: Someone who could still leave a room.
Someone I needed to become.
responses: You did not need to ask permission then.
You have been looking for him in the glass ever since.

second.question: If I break it, will you stop hearing that voice?
choices: No. It is here even when you are silent.
Break it and we will find out.
responses: You are beginning to listen.
You tried that once. You kept every piece.

first.question: Nine lives. You buried eight under a title.
choices: The scarf. The river. Those were my memories.
You cannot know what I was before this room.
responses: You kept calling us strangers so you would not have to remember.
I remember the name you stopped answering to.

quiet.remembered: The lantern was beside your first bed. Before the street, the sea, the crown.

second.question: When you say you do not know me, who are you trying to forget?
choices: The one I was before anyone needed a king.
The one who believed the crown would be enough.
responses: He is still waiting for you to turn around.
He is the one who opened the door to us.

second.question: Why does this small flame frighten you more than my spear?
choices: I remember that room. I remember being small.
Because I cannot command it to go out.
responses: Then hold on to that. There was a name before Majesty.
You tried. It burned inside you instead.

first.question: Morrow. Before anyone called you Majesty.
choices: I remember that name.
No one living knows that name.
responses: Every cat who came here was one of your earlier lives. The crown kept us inside you.
We are your earlier lives, Morrow. The crown shut us inside you. You called us strangers.

patchwork.remembered: The scarf was yours. The chain was yours. Every hand that raised a weapon was yours.

second.question: What did you think would happen to all the lives you refused to let end?
choices: I thought I could keep them safe.
I thought I could bear it.
responses: You locked the door from the inside. I am not leaving you behind it.
Then face me. No title between us.

second.question: Will you answer when I call you Morrow?
choices: Yes. I will answer to my own name.
You will have to reach me first.
responses: Then look at me. I have waited long enough.
I know where your heart is. I remember it beating.
